mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a high-inflation shock.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 exceeding 2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or GDP growth recovers above trend within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in UNRATE above 4.0% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered months, or inflation does not accelerate in the same period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below 98 for three consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate sales and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or industrial production rebounds above trend within one month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS and a fall in CPIAUCSL (both outside their 5-year median ranges) signals a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with disinflation, which increases risk aversion and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or inflation unexpectedly accelerates.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly increase in both GDPC1 and HOUST above their 3-month moving averages signals strengthening housing and overall demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or housing demand weakens within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in PAYEMS below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 12-mo MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or labor market indicators rebound within two months.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS is below 1.5% and CPIAUCSL is rising above 3% YoY for three consecutive months, the real interest rate becomes negative, incentivizing risk-taking and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1.5% AND CPIAUCSL YoY > 3% for three consecutive months
regime_hint: zero lower bound with rising inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or inflation fails to sustain above 3%.
